Exam-style practice

Self-check questions

Write your answer first. Then open the answer and mark it against the mark points.

A Circuits

A1 Model railway lamps

A model railway has two platform lamps, L1 (30 Ω) and L2 (60 Ω), in parallel.

A 25 Ω resistor is in series with the two lamps.

The supply is 9.0 V.

(a) Calculate the total resistance of the circuit. 3 marks

(b) Calculate the current supplied by the battery. 3 marks

Show the answer

(a)

Rp = (30 × 60) / (30 + 60) = 20 Ω

Rt = 20 + 25

Rt = 45 Ω

  • 1 mark for the parallel calculation (substitution or Rp = 20 Ω).
  • 1 mark for adding the 25 Ω resistor.
  • 1 mark for the answer with unit.

(b)

V = I R

9.0 = I × 45

I = 9.0 / 45

I = 0.20 A

  • 1 mark for substitution.
  • 1 mark for transposition.
  • 1 mark for the answer with unit.

A2 Bike light LED

A bike light has an LED in series with a resistor.

The supply is 9.0 V.

The LED needs 2.0 V across it and a current of 20 mA.

(a) Calculate the resistance of the series resistor. 3 marks

(b) Explain why the LED needs a resistor in series with it. 2 marks

Show the answer

(a)

VR = 9.0 − 2.0 = 7.0 V

V = I R

7.0 = 0.020 × R

R = 350 Ω

  • 1 mark for the voltage across the resistor.
  • 1 mark for substitution (current in amps).
  • 1 mark for the answer with unit.

(b)

The resistor limits the current through the LED …

… so the LED is not damaged.

  • 1 mark for cause (limits the current).
  • 1 mark for effect (stops the LED being damaged).

B Voltage dividers and sensors

B1 Frost alarm

A frost alarm warns a gardener when the temperature falls to 0 °C.

The sensing circuit is a resistor R above an NTC thermistor. Vin is measured across the thermistor. The supply is 9.0 V.

The table shows the thermistor's resistance.

  • −10 °C: 26 kΩ
  • −5 °C: 20 kΩ
  • 0 °C: 15 kΩ
  • 5 °C: 11 kΩ
  • 10 °C: 8.5 kΩ

(a) State the resistance of the thermistor at 0 °C. 1 mark

(b) The alarm is designed to switch on when Vin reaches 5.0 V. Calculate the resistance of R. Use your answer to part (a). 4 marks

Show the answer

(a)

15 kΩ (15 000 Ω)

  • 1 mark for the value with unit.

(b)

VR = 9.0 − 5.0 = 4.0 V

V1 / V2 = R1 / R2

4.0 / 5.0 = R / 15 000

R = (4.0 × 15 000) / 5.0

R = 12 000 Ω (12 kΩ)

  • 1 mark for the voltage across R.
  • 1 mark for substitution.
  • 1 mark for transposition.
  • 1 mark for the answer with unit.

B2 Helmet lights

A cycle helmet has a front LED and a rear LED that switch on when it gets dark.

The sensing circuit is a resistor above an LDR. Vin is measured across the LDR and goes to a transistor switch.

Describe the operation of this circuit as it gets darker. Include the resistance of the LDR, the voltage Vin, the transistor and both outputs. 5 marks

Show the answer

Answer

The resistance of the LDR increases.

Vin increases.

The transistor switches on.

The front LED lights.

The rear LED lights.

  • 1 mark for each link, in order. Apply follow-through.
  • A link that goes the wrong way loses that mark only.

C Transistors, relays and diodes

C1 Pond pump

A pond pump switches on when the water gets warm.

A sensing circuit drives a transistor. The transistor switches a relay. The relay switches the pump, which has its own supply.

(a) State the function of the transistor. 1 mark

(b) Describe why a relay is needed to switch the pump. 2 marks

(c) State the function of the base resistor. 1 mark

Show the answer

(a)

It acts as an (electronic) switch.

  • 1 mark.

(b)

The transistor can only switch a small current …

… the relay lets this small current switch the large current the pump needs (from its own supply).

  • 1 mark for the small current in the transistor / sensing circuit.
  • 1 mark for switching the large current / separate supply of the pump.

(c)

It limits the current into the base of the transistor.

  • 1 mark. Accept: protects the transistor from a large base current.

C2 Protection diode

The circuit shows a transistor switching a relay coil.

A protection diode is connected across the relay coil.

(a) Describe how the diode must be connected. 2 marks

(b) Explain the purpose of the diode. 2 marks

(c) Name the three connections of the transistor. 1 mark

Show the answer

(a)

Across (in parallel with) the relay coil …

… reverse biased: the bar (cathode) points to the positive supply.

  • 1 mark for position.
  • 1 mark for orientation.

(b)

When the relay switches off, the coil produces a large reverse (back) voltage …

… the diode carries this away, so the transistor is not damaged.

  • 1 mark for cause (back voltage from the coil).
  • 1 mark for effect (protects the transistor).

(c)

Base, collector and emitter.

  • 1 mark for all three.

D Systems

D1 Hand dryer sub-systems

An automatic hand dryer has four sub-systems: a light sensor, a control circuit, a fan motor and a heater.

(a) State which sub-system is the process. 1 mark

(b) Describe how the system boundary is shown on a sub-system diagram. 1 mark

(c) Describe the purpose of the system boundary. 1 mark

Show the answer

(a)

The control circuit.

  • 1 mark.

(b)

A dashed line drawn round all the sub-systems.

  • 1 mark.

(c)

It separates what is inside the system from the inputs and outputs outside it.

  • 1 mark for containing / separating the system from what is outside.

D2 Hand dryer input

In the hand dryer, a hand blocks light from reaching an LDR.

The LDR is the bottom resistor of a voltage divider. Vin is measured across the LDR.

Describe the operation of the input sub-system as a hand blocks the light. Make reference to the resistance of the LDR and the voltage Vin. 2 marks

Show the answer

Answer

The resistance of the LDR increases …

… so Vin increases.

  • 1 mark for LDR resistance increasing.
  • 1 mark for Vin increasing.

E Energy

E1 Patio heater

A patio heater runs from a 230 V supply. The current is 8.0 A.

(a) Calculate the power of the heater. 2 marks

(b) In one evening the heater gives out 900 000 J of useful heat. It is 0.75 (75 %) efficient. Calculate the input energy. 3 marks

Show the answer

(a)

P = V I

P = 230 × 8.0

P = 1840 W

  • 1 mark for substitution.
  • 1 mark for the answer with unit.

(b)

η = Eout / Ein

0.75 = 900 000 / Ein

Ein = 900 000 / 0.75

Ein = 1 200 000 J

  • 1 mark for substitution.
  • 1 mark for transposition.
  • 1 mark for the answer with unit.

E2 Sandwich press

A sandwich press heats two aluminium plates.

  • mass of the plates: 0.60 kg
  • specific heat capacity of aluminium: 900 J kg−1 °C−1
  • heat energy given to the plates: 27 000 J

(a) Calculate the rise in temperature of the plates. 3 marks

(b) Explain how the efficiency of the sandwich press could be improved. 2 marks

Show the answer

(a)

Eh = c m ΔT

27 000 = 900 × 0.60 × ΔT

ΔT = 27 000 / (900 × 0.60)

ΔT = 50 °C

  • 1 mark for substitution.
  • 1 mark for transposition.
  • 1 mark for the answer with unit.

(b)

Insulate the outside of the press / the lid …

… so less heat energy is lost to the surroundings.

  • 1 mark for cause, linked to the sandwich press.
  • 1 mark for effect.

F Contexts

F1 Electric wheelchair

A team is designing a new electric wheelchair.

Describe two tasks the electronic engineer would carry out in this project. 2 marks

Show the answer

Answer

Design the circuit that controls the motors.

Choose the sensors, such as an obstacle sensor.

Write the program for the microcontroller.

Test the circuit by simulation, then on a prototype.

  • 1 mark for each task, up to 2. It must be an electronics task.

F2 Electric car

A family replaces its petrol car with an electric car.

(a) Describe one positive economic impact of this change for the family. 1 mark

(b) Describe one negative economic impact of this change for the family. 1 mark

Show the answer

(a)

Charging costs less than petrol, so running costs fall.

  • 1 mark.

(b)

The electric car (and a home charger) costs more to buy.

  • 1 mark.

A Circuits

1. An ammeter measures the current through one lamp in a parallel circuit. How is it connected?

2. A 40 Ω resistor and a 10 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?

3. A 9.0 V supply is connected across a 45 Ω resistor. What is the current?

4. A shop sign has three lamps in parallel. One lamp is removed. What happens?

B Voltage dividers and sensors

5. An LDR is the bottom resistor of a voltage divider. Vin is measured across the LDR. It gets darker. What happens?

6. A voltage divider has R1 = 30 kΩ (top) and R2 = 20 kΩ (bottom) across a 5.0 V supply. What is the voltage across R2?

7. In a frost alarm, a variable resistor VR is above a thermistor. Vin is measured across the thermistor. The alarm must switch on at a higher temperature. What change should be made?

8. Two resistors are in series across a supply. The output is taken from the point between them. What is this arrangement called?

C Transistors, relays and diodes

9. What is the function of the transistor in a sensing circuit?

10. What are the three connections of a transistor?

11. Why is a diode connected across a relay coil?

12. How must the protection diode be connected?

D Systems

13. What is the purpose of the system boundary on a sub-system diagram?

14. In an automatic hand dryer, which part is the process sub-system?

15. What do the arrows between blocks on a sub-system diagram show?

16. In a frost alarm, which is the input sub-system?

E Energy

17. A hairdryer runs from a 230 V supply with a current of 5.0 A. What is its power?

18. A motor is supplied with 40 000 J. It is 0.85 (85 %) efficient. What is the useful output energy?

19. A camping kettle gives 50 160 J of heat to 0.40 kg of water (c = 4180 J kg−1 °C−1). What is the rise in temperature?

20. Which change would improve the efficiency of an electric heater in a garden office?
